parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Activity type(s), comma-separated. Accepted values: `TRADE`, `SPLIT`,
`MERGE`, `REDEEM` (automatic redemptions included), `CONVERSION`,
`MIGRATION`, `REWARD`, `YIELD`, `MAKER_REBATE`, `TAKER_REBATE`,
`REFERRAL_REWARD`, `DEPOSIT`, `WITHDRAWAL`, `DIRECTIONAL_SPLIT`,
`DIRECTIONAL_MERGE`, `THRESHOLD_COMPOSE`, `THRESHOLD_DECOMPOSE`, `TIP`.
Any other value is rejected with `400`. Omitted, the feed returns every
type except `TIP`.

`DEPOSIT` and `WITHDRAWAL` rows are returned only with
`exclude_deposits_withdrawals=false`. Under its default (`true`) they are
dropped even when named here, so `type=DEPOSIT` or `type=WITHDRAWAL`
alone returns an empty page.

`DIRECTIONAL_SPLIT`, `DIRECTIONAL_MERGE`, `THRESHOLD_COMPOSE` and
`THRESHOLD_DECOMPOSE` are operations on range events, whose outcomes are
value buckets and whose lines are ABOVE / BELOW positions over those
buckets. A directional split turns collateral plus the buckets between
two lines into ABOVE the lower line and BELOW the higher one; a
directional merge reverses it. Both are rows of the whole event, so a
`condition` filter never returns them. A threshold compose turns buckets
into one line position and a threshold decompose turns it back; these
rows carry the line's market and side. Split, merge, redeem and
conversion on a range event keep `SPLIT`, `MERGE`, `REDEEM` and
`CONVERSION`.

`TIP` is **opt-in**: it is never in the default set, so it is only
returned when you name it here. A tip is a user↔user pUSD transfer that
is not a trade-settlement leg; `size` is the amount and `side` carries the
direction (`IN` received / `OUT` sent).

endpoints.summary: List positions for a user or market

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The wallet to anchor on. At least one of `user`/`condition` is required.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Condition id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values). With
`user`, narrows that user's positions (all ids honoured). Without
`user`, anchors on the market's holders; exactly one id is accepted
there, and a multi-id list is rejected rather than silently truncated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: First-page size. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied (the cursor's size wins).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`. It
carries the page position, page size, and the status/sort/direction it
was minted under.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
One of `OPEN`, `REDEEMABLE`, `REDEEMABLE_LOST`, `MERGEABLE`, or `CLOSED`;
defaults to `OPEN`. `REDEEMABLE_LOST` requires `user`, supports all six
sorts, and defaults to `CURRENT_VALUE`; it preserves row status
`REDEEMABLE`. `MERGEABLE` is `OPEN` narrowed to live complementary pairs
(conditions where the wallet holds >= 2 servable-live tokens) and defaults
to `TOKENS`; it is user-scoped, so a market-anchored request renders as
`OPEN`.

`OPEN` is the superset; it includes settled-but-unredeemed winners,
which `REDEEMABLE` narrows to. `CLOSED` is exited positions.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description:
Event id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values).
User-anchored only.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description:
Case-insensitive market-title substring filter, honoured on every
anchor and status. SQL LIKE wildcards (`%`, `_`) keep their usual
meaning; empty or whitespace-only is treated as absent; at most 200
characters. NOT carried by the cursor: re-send it on every page of a
walk (like `condition` and the `start`/`end` window), or the cohort
silently widens.

parameters.name: filter_type
parameters.description:
`CASH` or `TOKENS`; defaults to `TOKENS` (the /v2/trades-homogenized
filter pair, replacing the former `size_threshold`).

parameters.name: filter_amount
parameters.description:
The filter floor. `TOKENS`: minimum CURRENT holding in shares
(defaults to the 0.1 dust floor; applies to `OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`; a
user's `CLOSED` set is not narrowed by it, and on a market anchor it
moves the OPEN/CLOSED boundary). `CASH`: minimum mark-to-market
`current_value` in USDC, on top of the token dust floor. Invalid
values fall back to the default.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description:
Also include positions on archived markets; defaults to `false`.
`OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`/`REDEEMABLE_LOST`/`MERGEABLE` only; combining it with
`status=CLOSED` is rejected. Inactive markets remain excluded either way.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
One of `CURRENT_VALUE`, `PRICE`, `TOKENS`, `UNREALIZED_PNL`,
`REALIZED_PNL`, `TOTAL_PNL`, or `TIMESTAMP` (the row's `last_event_at`).
`PRICE` ranks by the response's effective `current_price` on every
supported anchor and status. On `REDEEMABLE`, the existing winners-first
partition remains ahead of the requested price order. The default
follows the status: `CURRENT_VALUE` for `OPEN`/`REDEEMABLE`,
`REALIZED_PNL` for `CLOSED`. On a user's `CLOSED` positions, `TOKENS`,
`CURRENT_VALUE`, `PRICE` and `UNREALIZED_PNL` describe a holding that no
longer exists, so those pages are served in `REALIZED_PNL` order.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Inclusive lower bound on `last_event_at`, epoch seconds; omit or `0` for
unbounded (the `/v2/activity` + `/v2/trades` vocabulary).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Inclusive upper bound on `last_event_at`, epoch seconds; omit or `0` for
unbounded.

A position with no native economics carries no `last_event_at` and is
therefore **excluded by any bound**, in either direction; a window asks
which positions moved inside it, and a row with no clock has no answer.
Unbounded requests still serve those rows.

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: `ASC` or `DESC`; defaults to `DESC`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The wallet to anchor on. Required; combo positions are user-anchored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: First-page size. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied (the cursor's size wins).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Combo condition id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values).
`condition_id` / `conditionId` are accepted aliases.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
One of `OPEN`, `REDEEMABLE`, `PARTIAL`, `RESOLVED_WIN`, `RESOLVED_LOSS`,
`RESOLVED_PARTIAL`; default (absent) is the held-visibility listing.

Aligned with `/v2/positions`: `OPEN` is the superset; it includes
still-held redeemable positions; and `REDEEMABLE` narrows to exactly
the rows whose `redeemable` flag is `true`. `REDEEMABLE` must be the
sole value; the other values may be combined comma-separated and keep
per-value equality semantics.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
`FIRST_ENTRY` (default, except under `status=REDEEMABLE`, which defaults
to `ENTRY_COST` so the largest claims lead) | `ENTRY_COST` |
`CURRENT_VALUE` (alias of `ENTRY_COST`) | `UPDATED`. `FIRST_ENTRY DESC`
and `UPDATED ASC` page by keyset; every other combination pages by an
offset-shaped cursor. The minted cursor binds sort + direction along
with the `status`/`condition` cohort, so a page-2 request needs only
`?user=` and `?cursor=`; restating a filter is allowed but must agree.

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: `ASC` or `DESC` (default `DESC`).

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description:
Incremental-sync watermark: INCLUSIVE lower bound on `updated_at`,
epoch seconds. Without a `status` filter, either watermark serves the
sync view; every live row (mirror-complete), not only the held
listing; a `status` filter keeps its own row visibility. The window's
upper end is always capped by a short stability ceiling (about 90
seconds behind now), so a bound in the future cannot serve rows that
may still move.

parameters.name: updated_before
parameters.description:
Incremental-sync watermark: INCLUSIVE upper bound on `updated_at`,
epoch seconds; must not precede `updated_after`. See `updated_after`
for the sync-view and ceiling semantics.

parameters.name: token_id
parameters.description:
Outcome token id (the CLOB asset id the chart is keyed by). Required.
`tokenId` is an accepted alias.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Window start, epoch seconds, INCLUSIVE. Alone it means "up to the
present", and is capped at 15 days back from now.

Pass `end` too when paging: a window that tracks the present keeps
growing at the tip, and the 15-day cap is re-checked on every page, so a
walk that starts near the cap can outlive it.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Window end, epoch seconds, EXCLUSIVE. Requires `start`; on its own it
would ask for every point ever recorded up to `end`.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description:
Relative window INSTEAD of `start`/`end`: `max`, `all`, `1m`, `1w`,
`1d`, `6h`, `1h`, matched case-sensitively. An empty `interval=` is a
malformed value, not an absent one.

`max`/`all` serve the market's WHOLE life (back to 2022 for the oldest
markets) at 12-hour buckets by default; at `bucket_seconds` of 10800 or
43200 the window is unbounded, while finer widths keep a 30-day window.
The other intervals take a width sized to their own span when
`bucket_seconds` is omitted (`1h`/`6h`/`1d` 60, `1w` 300, `1m` 1800), and
each still floors an explicit value: 600 for `max`/`all`/`1m`, 300 for
`1w`.

parameters.name: bucket_seconds
parameters.description:
Bucket width in SECONDS (60…86400). `bucketSeconds` is an accepted alias.

OMIT it and the server sizes the width to the window: the finest tier
grain (60, 300, 1800, 10800, 43200) that keeps the series under ~2,500
points, except that an explicit window wider than 12 hours never
defaults to the 60s grain (send `bucket_seconds=60` when you want
second-by-minute detail over a longer window), and coarsened further if
that grain no longer reaches the window's start.
So a window up to 12 hours keeps 1-minute detail, half a day through a
week defaults to 300, fifteen days to 1800; interval presets keep their
own span-derived defaults (`1d` 60s, `1w` 300, `1m` 1800, and the
unbounded `max`/`all` 43200).

SEND it and it is served exactly as asked, which for a window older than
that resolution's retention means an empty page rather than a silent
substitution. An explicit value is also floored per interval: 600 for
`max`/`all`/`1m`, 300 for `1w`.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description:
Point-in-time read, epoch seconds, INCLUSIVE: the latest observation at
or before this instant. Cannot be combined with a window. `asOf` is an
accepted alias.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
First-page size; defaults to the cap (10,000). Ignored when `cursor` is
supplied (the cursor's size wins).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: question_id
parameters.description: One UMA question identifier (`0x` plus 64 hexadecimal characters).

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Comma-separated condition identifiers (at most 20 distinct values): the
Gamma condition id, or the structural condition id that `/v2/activity`
and `/v2/trades` serve before a market is listed.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Comma-separated positive Gamma event IDs (at most 20 distinct values).

parameters.name: token_id
parameters.description:
Token id(s), comma-separated (at most 50 distinct values): decimal
ERC-1155 ids as they appear on receipts and on the `token_id` and
`asset` fields of the other routes. Elements are trimmed, leading zeros
stripped and duplicates collapsed to their first position. `token_ids`
is an accepted alias. Exactly one of `token_id` and `condition` is
required.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Condition selector(s), comma-separated (at most 10 distinct values),
each `0x` followed by 62 or 64 hex digits: a ConditionalTokens
condition id (for a market carried over to polymarket-v2, its whole
family), a neg-risk market id (every market of the structure), a
polymarket-v2 condition id (that condition only), the 66-character
condition id of a native polymarket-v2 market, or the on-chain event
id of a polymarket-v2 neg-risk structure (every question of it).
Elements are trimmed, lower-cased and duplicates collapsed to their
first position. `condition_id` and `conditionId` are accepted aliases.
Exactly one of `token_id` and `condition` is required.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Address to filter by; omit for the market/event/global feed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: First-page size. Ignored when `cursor` is supplied (the cursor's size wins).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: taker_only
parameters.description:
Defaults to `true`: each fill is served once, on its taker side.
`false` includes the maker rows too.

parameters.name: filter_type
parameters.description: CASH or TOKENS; defaults to TOKENS.

parameters.name: filter_amount
parameters.description: Minimum trade size; defaults to 0.01, and 0 means the same.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Window start on `block_timestamp`, epoch seconds (inclusive); honored
on the `user` shape only. Omitted or `0` floors to three years back;
`start=1` asks for full history. The `condition`/`event_id` shapes
serve a fixed three-year window and the bare feed the rolling
current-plus-previous month, ignoring both bounds.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Window end, epoch seconds (inclusive); honored on the `user` shape
only; omitted or `0` means now plus one day.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Condition id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values).
`condition_id` / `conditionId` are accepted aliases.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Event id(s), comma-separated (at most 20 distinct values).

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: BUY or SELL.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Proxy wallet. The `user_address` spelling is accepted as an alias.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Window: `max`, `all`, `1m`, `1w`, `1d`, `12h`, or `6h`. Defaults to `1d`.

parameters.name: fidelity
parameters.description: Output grid: `1d`, `18h`, `12h`, `3h`, or `1h`. Defaults to `1h`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description:
The wallet whose profile stats to return. Required; `0x` followed by
40 hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The wallet whose volume to return. Required.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description:
Window start, epoch seconds, inclusive. Omitted or `0` disables the
bound (the feeds' convention). Volume is tracked in whole UTC days, so
the bound is floored to its UTC day.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description:
Window end, epoch seconds, inclusive, floored to its UTC day. Omitted
or `0` disables the bound.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The wallet whose portfolio value to return. Required.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description:
Comma-separated `condition_id`s (at most 20 distinct values); omit for
the full portfolio.
